ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High-contrast bimodal distribution. Approximately 60% of pixels in the visible fluke area reside in the high-intensity (white) spectrum, primarily in the central lobe regions, with 40% in the low-intensity (black/dark grey) spectrum localized at the margins and peduncle junction.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Large, contiguous high-intensity white blobs occupy the mid-to-upper interior of both lobes. Low-intensity black pixels form a continuous boundary along the trailing edge and tips, with dense inter-lobar black pigmentation extending from the peduncle in a dendritic pattern.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Acute V-shaped depression with a calculated internal pixel angle of approximately 52 degrees and a depth-to-width ratio of 1:1.2 relative to the immediate notch boundary.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency, low-amplitude serrations present along the left lobe trailing edge. The right lobe trailing edge exhibits a major macro-level geometric discontinuity: a deep, sub-rectangular notch/avulsion approximately 15% into the lobe depth.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Symmetrical upward-sweeping convex curve originating from the peduncle and terminating in sharp, slightly tapered distal tips.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Multiple high-intensity circular pixel clusters (diameters 3-8 pixels) are distributed near the distal tips and scattered across the black-pigmented areas, consistent with sessile organism attachment sites.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Extensive network of white, non-parallel linear pixel disruptions (rake marks) of varying widths (1-4 pixels) crossing the low-intensity regions of both lobes and the vertical peduncle surface.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Major trailing edge avulsion (missing tissue segment) on the right lobe. A distinct linear red-spectrum pixel cluster (chromatic anomaly) is visible on the upper quadrant of the left lobe, intersecting a white pigmentation zone.
other_distinctive_markers: Extremely high density of linear abrasions creates a complex, high-frequency textural pattern across the entire trailing half of the fluke's visible surface.
